hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? starting something where you know nothing? a new language, a new job, a new city.
options: then this festival is for you. watch.
keep this one for the next first day.

steps.line: In Kerala, there’s a beautiful day for beginners: Vidyarambham, the start of learning.
A little child sits in a lap. Someone holds their tiny finger, and helps them trace their first letters in a plate of rice.

steps.q: Some Kerala families travel far so one special kind of guide can hold their child’s finger. Who?
steps.why: At Thunchan Parambu, home of the poet Ezhuthachan, well-known writers guide first letters. Most often, though, it’s a priest, a teacher or an elder.

steps.q: The first words traced are often a short prayer. To whom?
steps.why: Often “Om Hari Sri Ganapataye Namah”: a bow to Ganesha, who clears the way at every beginning. The day itself belongs to Saraswati.

steps.line: Often the first words are a short prayer, and the day is sacred to Saraswati, the goddess of learning.

steps.q: Who else comes to begin learning that day?
o: Older kids about to start school
Teachers, to be blessed for the year
steps.why: Grown-ups too: anyone starting music, dance or anything new. Watch.

steps.line: Grown-ups come too: people who want to start music, or dance, or anything new.
Nobody laughs at the beginner. The whole temple celebrates them.

steps.q: Nobody laughs at the beginner. Why make such a fuss over a first wobbly letter?
o: Good luck on day one lasts all year
It honors the teacher more than the child
steps.why: Starting is the hardest step, so it gets the celebration. Here, being a beginner is sacred, not embarrassing.

steps.line: So go ahead and be a beginner. In Hinduism, the first wobbly letter gets a festival.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Besides the rice, an elder often traces the same letters somewhere else. Where?
o: On the child’s tongue, with gold
On the temple wall, in red powder
On a palm leaf the child keeps
steps.why: Often with a gold ring, on the tongue, so learning and speech begin golden. In many homes that comes first, then the rice.

say: here’s what i love. the first wobbly letter gets a festival.
in hinduism, being a beginner isn’t embarrassing. it’s sacred. you’re allowed to start small and clumsy.

steps.q: Vidyarambham usually falls on Vijayadashami, the day after the nine nights of Navratri. What does that day celebrate?
o: The start of a new year
steps.why: Vijayadashami means “the tenth day of victory.” Beginning to learn on a day of victory is part of the point.

today.say: start one thing you’ve been embarrassed to be a beginner at. do the first clumsy step today.
options: then your first wobbly letter counts. go.
that’s exactly who this festival is for. one step.
